definition: Behavior informatics (BI) is the informatics of behaviors so as to obtain behavior intelligence and behavior insights.
details: BI is a research method combining science and technology, specifically in the area of engineering. The purpose of BI includes analysis of current behaviors as well as the inference of future possible behaviors. This occurs through pattern recognition. Different from applied behavior analysis from the psychological perspective, BI builds computational theories, systems and tools to qualitatively and quantitatively model, represent, analyze, and manage behaviors of individuals, groups and/or organizations. BI is built on classic study of behavioral science, including behavior modeling, applied behavior analysis, behavior analysis, behavioral economics, and organizational behavior. Typical BI tasks consist of individual and group behavior formation, representation, computational modeling, analysis, learning, simulation, and understanding of behavior impact, utility, non-occurring behaviors, etc. for behavior intervention and management. The Behavior Informatics approach to data utilizes cognitive as well as behavioral data. By combining the data, BI has the potential to effectively illustrate the big picture when it comes to behavioral decisions and patterns. One of the goals of BI is also to be able to study human behavior while eliminating issues like self-report bias. This creates more reliable and valid information for research studies.

explainer.lead: Behavior informatics uses computational models to turn evidence about what people or groups do, together with cognitive data, into insight about behavior. These insights can explain current patterns, suggest possible future behavior, and support interventions without relying entirely on what people say about themselves.

tiers.eli5: It is like trying to understand why a football team plays the way it does: you watch what the players do and also consider what they are thinking, then look for repeated patterns. Behavior informatics uses computers to do this for people, groups, and organizations. The goal is to understand current behavior, anticipate what might happen next, and help guide useful changes.
tiers.practitioner: An engineering team would combine behavioral and cognitive data, then build computational models for representation, pattern analysis, learning, or simulation. The outputs can support analysis of present behavior, inference of possible future behavior, and intervention planning. A key pitfall is depending only on self-reports, since one aim of BI is to reduce self-report bias and improve reliability and validity.
tiers.paperLevel: BI comprises computational theories, systems, and tools for qualitatively and quantitatively modeling, representing, analyzing, and managing the behavior of individuals, groups, and/or organizations. Its tasks include behavior formation, representation, computational modeling, analysis, learning, simulation, and study of behavior impact, utility, and non-occurring behaviors. It uses pattern recognition to analyze current behavior and infer possible future behavior, distinguishing its computational approach from applied behavior analysis in psychology.

explainer.example: A team studying workplace collaboration combines records of how a group actually works with cognitive data, builds a computational model of its current collaboration patterns, and uses pattern recognition to infer possible future behavior before planning an intervention.

usedIn.name: Behavioral research
usedIn.detail: Combines cognitive and behavioral data to study decisions and patterns while aiming to reduce self-report bias.

usedIn.name: Behavior intervention and management
usedIn.detail: Uses behavior models and insights to inform interventions for individuals, groups, or organizations.

usedIn.name: Organizational behavior
usedIn.detail: Applies computational representation and analysis to behavior within groups and organizations.

explainer.intuition: Behavior becomes easier to understand when observed actions and cognitive data are examined together rather than treated as a stream of isolated events. BI builds computational representations of those behaviors so recurring patterns can be analyzed and possible future behaviors inferred.
howItWorks: Gather behavioral data together with cognitive data.
Represent and model individual, group, or organizational behavior computationally.
Analyze, learn from, or simulate the models to identify patterns.
Infer possible future behaviors and examine impact, utility, or non-occurring behaviors.
Use the resulting behavior intelligence and insights for intervention and management.
explainer.whyItMatters: Joining cognitive and behavioral data can give a fuller picture of behavioral decisions and patterns. It can also produce more reliable and valid research information by addressing problems such as self-report bias.
misconceptions: BI is not simply applied behavior analysis; it emphasizes computational theories, systems, and tools.
It does more than describe past actions: it also uses pattern recognition to infer possible future behaviors.
It does not rely only on records of actions, because its approach also incorporates cognitive data.
